sentences.text: Dysmoropelia dekarchiskos is the sole member of its genus, a monotypic group containing only this single species.
This extinct bird was a large dove belonging to the family Columbidae and the order Columbiformes, measuring approximately 31 cm in length.
It possessed short wings relative to its body size and robust legs, showing adaptations similar to other flightless Columbidae like the dodo, though these traits were less extreme.
The genus name Dysmoropelia comes from the Greek words dysmoros, meaning unfortunate, and pelia, meaning wild dove.
The species name dekarchiskos references Napoleon Bonaparte's exile to Saint Helena, deriving from Greek terms meaning leader of ten men and small cape.
The genus was formally described by Olson in 1975 based on fossils found at the Sugarloaf Hill locality.
The bird is presumed to have been hunted to extinction shortly after the island was discovered in 1502.
The bird was endemic to the island of Saint Helena in the South Atlantic Ocean, living between 0.129 and 0.0117 million years ago.
Fossils of the bird date to the Late Pleistocene and were discovered in aeolian calcareous sands at the Sugarloaf Hill locality.
